claude_proposed_widenings.name: ReactionTrigger.spell_targets_only_self_non_area
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The rod's reaction window depends on the triggering spell targeting only the wielder and not creating an area of effect; existing reaction triggers cannot express that predicate.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: you can take a Reaction to absorb a spell that is targeting only you and doesn't create an area of effect

claude_proposed_widenings.name: absorb_spell_energy_pool
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The item stores spell energy from canceled incoming spells, tracks current stored levels separately from lifetime absorbed total, and stops absorbing after 50 total levels. That is a different resource flow from existing charge pools.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: The absorbed spell's effect is canceled, and the spell's energy-not the spell itself-is stored in the rod. The rod can absorb and store up to 50 levels of energy over the course of its existence.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: spend_stored_energy_as_spell_slot
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The rod does not grant named spells; it substitutes stored energy for the wielder's own spell slots when casting spells they already know or have prepared.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: you can convert energy stored in it into spell slots to cast spells you have prepared or know. You use the stored levels in place of your slots but otherwise cast the spell as normal.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: ItemDestructionPolicy.nonmagical_when_absorption_exhausted_and_empty
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The rod becomes nonmagical only after its lifetime absorption capacity is exhausted and no energy remains stored, which is not covered by existing destruction policies.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: A rod that can no longer absorb spell energy and has no energy remaining becomes nonmagical.
